{{Quote|<nowiki />''[&hellip;]'' Contispex and his successors exploited prohuman sentiment for increasingly violent jihads on what was then its periphery. ''[&hellip;]'' "cold" and "hot" wars alternated for a thousand years ''[&hellip;]'' until Pius Dea rule met its end in that famous encounter which hardly needs retelling here.|Doctor Gabrel Treon, "Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes"|<ref name="TTSP">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref>}}
In [[10,966 BBY]], a '''battle''' took place at the celestial body [[Uquine/Legends|Uquine]] at the conclusion of the conflict known as the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict|Pius Dea Civil War]]. After the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had been under the control of the [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] [[Pius Dea]] cult for a [[Pius Dea Era|millennium]], an alliance between the [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]] [[Species/Legends|species]]; the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]; the independent [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] and its allies; and the former Pius Dea members known as the [[Renunciates]], who had converted to a secret anti-Pius Dea faith, plotted to overthrow the Republic regime.

The [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]], persuaded into joining the resistance, seeded Pius Dea [[cathedral ship]]s with rogue [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] code, which it activated a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the Renunciates had revealed themselves and opened a civil war against the Pius Dea Faithful. The Pius Dea [[Warship/Legends|warships]] were launched into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], with [[Starship/Legends|ships]] including the Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Contispex XIX]]'s [[Flame of Sinthara|vessel]] being deposited at Uquine, where a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of waiting Renunciate [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]] annihilated them. Meanwhile, the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] captured Contispex XIX, allowing for the subsequent end to the Pius Dea rule over the Republic.

==Prelude==
After the [[11,987 BBY]] election of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Contispex I/Legends|Contispex I]], who was a member of the [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] [[Pius Dea]] religious sect, the Republic rapidly came under the control of fanatical Pius Dea adherents. Contispex I and his [[Contispex dynasty|dynastic]] successor Chancellors initiated a series of [[Pius Dea Crusades|crusades]] spanning a [[Pius Dea Era|millennium]] and targeting [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Species/Legends|species]] at the borders of the Republic. Beginning around [[11,100 BBY]], Pius Dea [[Inquisition]]s also tried, condemnded, and [[Death/Legends|executed]] in mass trials those members of the Republic who were found to be "impure."<ref name="TEGtW" />

[[File:Bureau_of_Ships_and_Services.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The assistance rendered to the anti-Pius Dea alliance by the Bureau of Ships and Services made possible the capture of Supreme Chancellor Contispex XIX at Uquine.]]
In [[11,933 BBY]], the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the ancient protectors of the Republic, [[Recusal|declared]] itself no longer subject to Republic rule in protest against the actions of the Pius Dea. Approximately eight [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] later, members of the [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]] species approached the Order and convinced the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to end their isolation and help end the Pius Dea tyranny. The Caamasi, Jedi, and agents of the independent [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]] and its allies then began to spread a secret faith throughout the Pius Dea ranks, with the converted becoming the [[Renunciates]]. The Caamasi also persuaded the [[Bureau of Ships and Services/Legends|Bureau of Ships and Services]] (BoSS) to abandon its traditional neutrality to help<ref name="TEGtW" /> the secret anti-Pius Dea alliance that made its preparations over the course of a century.<ref name="Insider 133">{{InsiderCite|133|10 Key Battles}}</ref> Reasoning that Pius Dea was a [[Disease/Legends|disease]] that was ravaging [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="TEGtW" /> the Bureau of Ships and Services seeded the [[Memory bank/Legends|memory banks]] of Pius Dea [[cathedral ship]]s with rogue [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] code.<ref name="Insider 133" />

Finally, in [[10,967 BBY]], the Renunciates revealed themselves, igniting the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict|Pius Dea Civil War]] and fighting the Pius Dea Faithful with the help of Alsakani, the Jedi, and alien [[Navy/Legends|navies]]. A [[10,966 BBY|year later]],<ref name="TEGtW" /> when the Faithful appeared to be prevailing,<ref name="Insider 133" /> the BoSS activated the code aboard the Pius Dea [[Warship/Legends|warships]], causing thousands of them to jump into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Many of the [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] emerged in interstellar [[Realspace/Legends|space]] with their [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and communications systems disabled.<ref name="TEGtW" />

==The battle==
The ships of the Pius Dea vanguard, including ''[[Flame of Sinthara]]'' with Supreme Chancellor [[Contispex XIX]] aboard, instead emerged at the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] celestial body [[Uquine/Legends|Uquine]], where an immense [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of Renunciate [[Battleship/Legends|battleships]] awaited them. Caught off guard, the offensive and defensive systems of the cathedral ships had been rendered inoperative, and the Renunciates methodically destroyed the Pius Dea vessels. The Jedi also captured the Supreme Chancellor on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of their ship.<ref name="TEGtW" />

==Aftermath==
Contispex XIX was tried and [[Prisoner/Legends|imprisoned]], and Jedi [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Biel Ductavis]] became the Supreme Chancellor. Under Ductavis's leadership, the Pius Dea rule ended, and the [[Ductavis Era]], a [[Time/Legends|time]] period that lasted from approximately [[11,000 BBY]] to [[9000 BBY]]<ref name="TEGtW" /> and was known as an age of rebuilding for the Republic, began.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> During a series of meetings held at the world [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt]] after the victory at Uquine, Renunciate [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Pers Pradeux]] and his fellow [[Republic officer/Legends|officers]] reorganized and rebuilt the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]], which, by assisting in the overthrow of Contispex XIX, had restored some of its honor after having previously served the Pius Dea. In the process, Pradeux helped forge naval traditions that continued to last for [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]].<ref name="TEGtW" /> In [[104 ABY]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Gabrel Treon]] indirectly mentioned the battle at Uquine, characterizing it as a well-remembered "famous encounter," in the article "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]," published in the [[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]].<ref name="TTSP" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Essential_Guide_to_Warfare-cover.jpg|thumb|right|250px|''The Essential Guide to Warfare'' provided the first description of the battle at Uquine.]]
The "famous encounter" that ended the rule of Pius Dea over the Galactic Republic was mentioned in "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]," an article authored by [[Nathan O'Keefe]] and published as part of the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature on [[February 5]], [[2009]].<ref name="TTSP" /> O'Keefe intentionally left the mention vague so that the authors of future ''[[Star Wars]]'' novels or [[Star Wars comic books|comics]] could develop the event more fully.<ref name="TTSP Endnotes">{{Blog|valinkenobi|14/comments|TTSP Endnotes: Volume 1}}</ref> The battle was eventually described by the<ref name="TEGtW" /> [[April 3]], [[2012]]<ref name="Penguin-Paperback">{{PenguinRandomHouse|url=books/180097/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-star-wars-by-jason-fry-with-paul-r-urquhart/9780345477620|text=The Essential Guide to Warfare: Star Wars}}</ref> reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]].<ref name="TEGtW" />

The battle of Uquine was then featured in the article "[[10 Key Battles]]," authored by Fry and Urquhart and published in the [[Star Wars Insider 133|133rd]] issue of the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' magazine<ref name="Insider 133" /> on [[May 1]], 2012.<ref name="Titan">{{TitanMagazines|url=t/star-wars-insider/us/133|text=Star Wars Insider #133}}</ref> In the article, the battle was ranked fourth after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Insider 133" /> of the [[original trilogy]] films [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], respectively,<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> and the [[Battle of Ebaq]]<ref name="Insider 133" /> from the ''[[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order]]'' novel series.<ref name="DestinysWay">''[[The New Jedi Order: Destiny's Way]]''</ref>
